current_text.html: A clerk or clerks shall be elected by the Session, Presbytery, and General Assembly to serve for a definite period as determined by the court. It is the duty of the clerk, besides recording the transactions, to preserve the records carefully, and to grant extracts from them whenever properly required. Such extracts under the hand of the clerk shall be evidence to any ecclesiastical court, and to every part of the Church.

occurrences.excerpt: CCB advised that a stated clerk may provide information consistent with presbytery records, especially when requested by a former TE in connection with ecclesiastical litigation.

relationships.title: Certification of presbytery dismissal by committee chairman's letter

occurrences.excerpt: A letter from a presbytery committee chairman is insufficient evidence of dismissal; BCO 46-6 requires a certificate bearing the stated clerk's signature per BCO 10-4.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC denied RE Gerald Hedman's complaint against Pacific Northwest Presbytery, which had adopted five not-guilty judgments on charges that TE Peter Leithart's baptism, covenant, imputation, justification, and union-with-Christ views contradicted the Westminster Standards. Bound to the record and clear-error review, the SJC found no procedural violation and insufficient evidence that Presbytery clearly erred. It left the verdicts undisturbed, declined to endorse Leithart's views generally, and urged continued clarification of his non-standard terminology. A separate dissent would have found error and ordered a new trial or reference.

metadata.synopsis: The 40th General Assembly cited Korean Capital Presbytery for failing to respond to substantive exceptions in its October 6, 2008 minutes. The SJC noted that the Presbytery had submitted responses approved by the Presbytery under BCO 10-4 and found those responses acceptable. The record does not state a dismissal, acquittal, or other formal merits disposition; the matter is an administrative BCO 40-5 citation resolved by acceptance of the Presbytery's responses.

metadata.synopsis: The 39th General Assembly cited Warrior Presbytery under BCO 40 provisions for failing to answer exceptions of substance in several meeting minutes. The SJC recorded that the Presbytery had since submitted responses approved by the Presbytery and found them acceptable. The adopted ruling provides no further rationale or separate relief.

Pacific Presbytery was cited and appeared before the SJC regarding exceptions of substance found in its records; the SJC accepted the presbytery's response as acceptable, pending certification that the response was approved by the presbytery.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint by two ruling elders against Korean Eastern Presbytery over a disputed congregational meeting (three commissioners dissented). The session was deadlocked and had not called a requested meeting; KEP's administrative commission called and supervised the February 18, 2001 meeting, and KEP approved that action. The SJC reversed both lower-court actions, holding that BCO 25-2 places responsibility on the session and that the presbytery's proper course was to adjudicate a complaint under BCO 43, not act for the session. It declined to rule on the meeting's legal effect.

metadata.synopsis: In a dispute arising from a Korean Eastern Presbytery congregational election, two ruling elders were tried, refused to plead, and were suspended from sacraments and office; KEP denied their appeal, then increased the censures to deposition and excommunication for contumacy. The SJC affirmed KEP's denial and the guilt findings, but reversed the increased censures. An appellate court may not increase a censure under BCO 42-9; the trial court retains discretion to remove or increase an indefinite suspension, though the appellate court may recommend a lesser censure. The original suspension remained.
